advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only write the initial 'running' record for the LEADER (handle.is_new), or make the running write not overwrite an existing terminal record, so a follower cannot clobber a settled verdict.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:211-219 records `"status": "running", "started_at": time.time()` for EVERY start, including the follower branch (only `if handle.is_new` gates the daemon spawn, not the record write)
record_gate_run is last-writer-wins keyed by job_id: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:77 `(d / job_id).write_text(json.dumps(record), ...)`

_attach_or_create only returns a follower while the leader is not done (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:185), but the leader can settle (daemon finally: _mcp_llm.py:158-171 writes terminal then handle.complete) between begin_gate_job and the follower's record write
_resolve_status then sees no active daemon + fresh started_at within grace -> 'running', later 'stale-running' (gate_runs.py:125-130)
advisory.finding: A follower *_start (is_new=False, same job_id) unconditionally re-records status='running' with a fresh started_at; because the gate_runs index is last-writer-wins keyed by job_id, a duplicate start racing/after the leader daemon's terminal write clobbers the terminal 'passed'/'failed' record back to 'running', so gate_status misreports a settled run.
scenarios: A client re-fires *_start (the -32001 retry this feature targets) just as the first run completes: the shared job_id's terminal verdict is overwritten with 'running', and a subsequent gate_status poll reports running then stale-running for an already-completed run.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the initial record_gate_run behind `if handle.is_new:` (followers already share the leader's job_id and its record), or have record_gate_run refuse to downgrade a terminal status to 'running'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the git basis-resolve + index write on the *_start event-loop path stays sub-ms, or offload the blocking work so the async start cannot stall the loop.
evidence: review_plan_start / verify_completion_start are `async def` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:230, 273)
offload_sync_tools skips already-async tools: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:261 `if getattr(tool, "is_async", False): continue`
begin_gate_job calls resolve_basis_sha which imports rebar.llm.workflow.snapshot.resolve_sha (git resolve) — src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:96-99
record_gate_run does mkdir + write_text on the event loop (gate_runs.py:75-77)
advisory.finding: The async *_start tool bodies are `async def` and are therefore NOT offloaded to a worker thread (offload_sync_tools skips already-async tools), yet begin_gate_job resolves the basis SHA via git shell-out (resolve_basis_sha->resolve_sha) and record_gate_run does file I/O inline, running on the event loop and potentially blocking it despite the 'returns in ms' contract.
scenarios: A large repo / slow git ref resolution or slow disk makes the *_start call block the anyio event loop rather than returning in milliseconds.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>` index against the follower `running` write clobbering the leader's terminal record (skip the running re-record for `is_new=False`, or make record_gate_run refuse to downgrade a terminal status to running).
evidence: Shared resource: index file `(d / job_id).write_text(json.dumps(record), ...)` keyed by job_id — gate_runs.py:77; docstring 'last-writer-wins' gate_runs.py:65
Executor 1 (leader daemon): `threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True).start()` writing terminal status in finally — src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:169,182
Executor 2 (follower tool body on another anyio worker thread): module docstring 'the two overlapping gate calls are concurrent *threads*' — src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:23-24
WRITE (terminal): daemon finally `record_gate_run({... "status": status ...})` — src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:169-179
WRITE (running, unconditional for a follower): `_start_gate_job` `record_gate_run({... "status": "running", "started_at": time.time()})` runs before `if handle.is_new` — src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:211-221

Sibling accessor and its guard: both writers use the SAME unguarded `write_text`; there is no lock/transaction/atomic-rename around the index file, unlike the in-memory registry which IS serialized by `with _lock:` (_mcp_inflight.py:182) — the index file is the unlocked twin

Harm: a follower arriving after the leader daemon settled reverts the durable `passed`/`failed` handle back to `running` with a fresh `started_at`; `_resolve_status` then reports `running`/`stale-running` for a run that actually PASSED (gate_runs.py:121-130), a corrupted run handle a caller polling `gate_status(job_id)` branches on
advisory.finding: A duplicate `*_start` that attaches to an in-flight run (`is_new=False`) unconditionally re-writes the shared `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>` index with `status:"running"` and a fresh `started_at` AFTER the leader's daemon may have already recorded the terminal verdict, clobbering it (lost update). `_start_gate_job` calls `record_gate_run(... status:"running" ...)` at line 211 BEFORE the `if handle.is_new` guard at line 220, so a follower always re-records `running` for the shared job_id.
scenarios: Client hits -32001 timeout on review_plan_start, retries; the retry attaches as a follower just as the leader daemon finishes and records `passed`; the follower's `running` write lands last, so gate_status(job_id) reports running/stale-running for a passed run
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_start_gate_job`, only call `record_gate_run(status='running')` when `handle.is_new` (a follower must not re-record), or make `record_gate_run` a compare-and-set that refuses to overwrite a terminal status with `running` for the same job_id.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving `_terminal_from_result` (or the daemon) with a `{"error":...}` dict (=> failed) and a `{"verdict":"BLOCK"}` dict (=> passed/BLOCK).
evidence: Added: `if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("error"):\n        return "failed", result.get("error")` and `return "passed", verdict` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:139-142)

A regression collapsing BLOCK to `failed` (or error to `passed`) would go undetected — the only tool-level test uses `{"verdict": "PASS"}`.
advisory.finding: The `failed` and BLOCK classification branches of `_terminal_from_result` are never tested. No test passes an error-carrying result dict or a BLOCK verdict through the daemon's classifier.
scenarios: A gate run that BLOCKs is polled and its handle status is asserted

The daemon's `finally` records this terminal `failed` status to the durable index (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:168-176)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that signs a completion-verifier attestation and asserts verify_completion_status returns verdict='certified' with verified_at_sha and signed_at populated.
evidence: Added branch: `if sig.get("verified"):\n ... status["verdict"] = "certified" ... status["verified_at_sha"] = signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest)` (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:184-190)
Only test is `test_verify_completion_status_unsigned_without_an_attestation`, asserting `verdict == "unsigned"` (tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py:179-183)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion on the `durable` key of gate_run_status output for a plan-review/completion job whose attestation exists.
evidence: Added: `durable = _durable_verdict(gate_type, ticket_id, repo_root)\n        if durable is not None:\n            out["durable"] = durable` (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py in gate_run_status)
search_files for `durable` in the test file finds only docstring/comment/job-name uses ('durable-job'); no assertion reads `out["durable"]`

search_files for `verify_completion_start` in tests finds only the docstring at tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py:4 — no test invokes the tool
No test asserts the `graph` parameter flows into the variant/work, nor that verify_completion_start returns a running handle

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix verify_completion_status to read the LIST manifest (mirror _authoritative_manifest/_authoritative_head incl. op-cert signed_manifest) so verified_at_sha is populated for a certified attestation.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:189 `manifest = sig.get("manifest") if isinstance(sig.get("manifest"), dict) else None`

src/rebar/_signing_hmac.py:164 `"manifest": manifest,` where manifest = `raw_manifest if isinstance(raw_manifest, list) else []` (_signing_hmac.py:196) — the verify result's manifest is a LIST, never a dict

Reference impl src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py:229-232 uses `_authoritative_manifest(sig)` (returns a list, attest.py:389) then `signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest) or _authoritative_head(sig)`
verified_at_sha_from_manifest signature expects `list[str] | None` (src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:82)
blocking.finding: verify_completion_status never populates verified_at_sha because it guards the manifest with isinstance(sig.get('manifest'), dict), but verify_signature returns 'manifest' as a LIST, so the branch is dead and verified_at_sha stays None for a valid certified attestation.
scenarios: Any certified completion-verifier attestation polled via verify_completion_status / gate_status durable field: verified_at_sha is always None so the caller cannot see WHAT code the verify was bound to.
blocking.suggested_fix: Replace the dict guard with the plan_review_status logic: `manifest = _authoritative_manifest(sig); status['verified_at_sha'] = signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest) or _authoritative_head(sig)`.
